dedupe_keys.name: cso ireland data centres metered electricity consumption table mec02

description: Ireland's Central Statistics Office publishes official statistics on how much electricity data centres use, a rare national series measured from meters, not estimated. The CSO takes meter data from ESB Networks, examines around 2.5 million meters and identifies the meter point reference numbers mainly used for data centre activity, then totals their consumption by quarter and year and compares it with households and other customers. The 2025 release, published on 7 July 2026, reports that data centres used 7,663 GWh in 2025, up 10 per cent from 6,973 GWh in 2024, and 23 per cent of all metered electricity, up from 5 per cent in 2015; quarterly use rose from 291 GWh in the first quarter of 2015 to 1,991 GWh in the last quarter of 2025, without the winter peaks seen for households. Coverage: Ireland, quarterly from 2015. Format and access: PxStat table MEC02 and the national open data portal in CSV, JSON-stat, PX and XLSX, free under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: national totals only, with no breakdown by site or region to protect confidentiality; the meter classification is the CSO's own. Simulation uses: demand baselines and growth scenarios for data-centre load in power system models, grid adequacy studies and interdependency analysis in a country where data centres are a large share of demand. Related records: the German data centre register and the EU data centre energy performance database report per-facility energy use.
